chip: Le long bras de la Chine
title: 12. La Chine veut que ses lois s'appliquent partout
gist: China has long resented the US for enforcing its laws abroad through sanctions, but is now doing the same — most strikingly by forcing Meta to unwind a $2bn AI acquisition in April. The shift traces back to the 2018 arrest of a Huawei executive in Canada at America's request, after which China built a body of extraterritorial law: a 2021 anti-sanctions law now being used to sue JPMorgan and Citigroup in Chinese courts, and conflicting London/Chinese court rulings that leave firms like Samsung caught between two legal systems. China is also using new laws to police criticism of itself abroad, part of a broader push to centralize control and stop being, in its own telling, a victim of world history rather than its maker.

body.fr: Pendant longtemps, la Chine a {{critiqué|criticized}} les pays étrangers qui appliquaient leurs propres lois sur son territoire.

bd.meaning: For a long time, China criticized foreign countries that applied their own laws on its territory.
chunks: that applied their own laws (qui = that/which)
bd.key: Past = avoir + past participle. a critiqué = “criticized” — the familiar avoir + past-form pattern.

body.fr: Mais aujourd'hui, la Chine fait la même chose : elle veut appliquer ses lois {{en dehors de|outside of}} ses frontières.

bd.meaning: But today, China is doing the same thing: it wants to apply its laws outside its borders.
chunks: la Chine fait la même chose
China does/is doing the same thing
it wants to apply its laws (vouloir + plain verb)
bd.key: vouloir + plain verb = “to want to ___.” veut appliquer = “wants to apply” — another helper-plus-plain-verb pair.

body.fr: En avril, la Chine a {{obligé|forced}} Meta, le propriétaire de Facebook, à annuler un achat de 2 milliards de dollars.

bd.meaning: In April, China forced Meta, Facebook's owner, to cancel a $2 billion purchase.
chunks: En avril, la Chine a obligé
in April, China forced (obliger qqn à = to force someone to)
un achat de 2 milliards de dollars
bd.key: obliger qqn à + plain verb = “to force someone to ___.” Same shape as aider qqn à and pousser qqn à — a person, à, then the plain verb.

body.fr: Meta voulait acheter Manus, une entreprise d'IA, mais le gouvernement chinois a dit non.

bd.meaning: Meta wanted to buy Manus, an AI company, but the Chinese government said no.
chunks: Meta wanted to buy Manus (voulait = imperfect of vouloir)
mais le gouvernement chinois a dit non
but the Chinese government said no
bd.key: “voulait” = “wanted” (an ongoing past state). Different from a voulu — voulait paints the wanting as a background situation, not a single completed action.

bd.meaning: This turning point comes from a specific event.
chunks: a specific event (précis after the noun)
bd.key: venir de + noun = “to come from ___.” A simple way to point back at a cause.

body.fr: En 2018, une {{directrice|(female) executive}} de Huawei a été arrêtée au Canada, à la demande des États-Unis.

bd.meaning: In 2018, a Huawei executive was arrested in Canada, at the request of the United States.
chunks: was arrested (être + past participle = the passive)
at the request of the United States
bd.key: être + past participle = the passive (“was ___ed”). a été arrêtée = “was arrested” — the participle agrees in gender, so it gets an extra -e for “une directrice.”

body.fr: Les dirigeants chinois ont compris que leurs entreprises étaient très {{vulnérables|vulnerable}} face aux lois américaines.

bd.meaning: Chinese leaders understood that their companies were very vulnerable to American laws.
chunks: Les dirigeants chinois ont compris que
their companies were very vulnerable (étaient = imperfect of être)
in the face of American laws
bd.key: “étaient” describes a past state, while ont compris is the single moment of realizing it — two different past tenses working together.

body.fr: Depuis 2021, la Chine a une loi contre les entreprises qui {{respectent|comply with}} les sanctions étrangères.

bd.meaning: Since 2021, China has had a law against companies that comply with foreign sanctions.
chunks: Depuis 2021, la Chine a une loi
since 2021, China has had a law
bd.key: depuis + present tense, again. depuis 2021, la Chine a = “since 2021, China has had” — French keeps the present where English switches to “has had.”

body.fr: Par exemple, deux grandes banques américaines, JPMorgan et Citigroup, sont {{poursuivies|sued}} devant un tribunal chinois.

bd.meaning: For example, two big American banks, JPMorgan and Citigroup, are being sued in a Chinese court.
chunks: Par exemple, deux grandes banques américaines
for example, two big American banks
are being sued (être + past participle, passive again)
bd.key: être + past participle, once more. sont poursuivies = “are (being) sued” — the same passive shape as a été arrêtée, now present tense and feminine plural.

body.fr: Elles doivent payer 44 millions de dollars, parce qu'elles ont {{gelé|frozen}} l'argent d'une entreprise chinoise sanctionnée par les États-Unis.

bd.meaning: They have to pay $44 million, because they froze the money of a Chinese company sanctioned by the US.
chunks: Elles doivent payer 44 millions de dollars
they have to pay $44 million (devoir + plain verb)
the money of a Chinese company
bd.key: devoir + plain verb = “have to.” doivent payer = “have to pay” — the same shape as doit payer from an earlier story, now plural.

body.fr: Cette situation crée un vrai problème pour les entreprises {{internationales|international}}.

bd.meaning: This situation creates a real problem for international companies.
chunks: a real problem (vrai before the noun)
bd.key: “vrai” before the noun, as you've seen before — a handful of common adjectives (vrai, bon, grand, petit) go before rather than after.

body.fr: En mai, un tribunal à Londres et un tribunal en Chine ont donné deux décisions {{différentes|different}} dans un même conflit entre Samsung et ZTE.

bd.meaning: In May, a court in London and a court in China gave two different rulings in the same dispute between Samsung and ZTE.
chunks: En mai, un tribunal à Londres
in May, a court in London
dans un même conflit entre Samsung et ZTE
in the same dispute between Samsung and ZTE
bd.key: “en Chine” vs “à Londres.” Countries use en, cities use à — two different little words for “in.”

body.fr: Samsung doit maintenant choisir : {{obéir|obey}} au tribunal anglais, ou obéir au tribunal chinois.

bd.meaning: Samsung now has to choose: obey the English court, or obey the Chinese court.
chunks: Samsung now has to choose (devoir + plain verb)
obey the English court (obéir à = to obey)
bd.key: obéir à = “to obey.” A fixed pairing — in French you always “obey TO” someone, with à.

body.fr: La Chine utilise aussi ses nouvelles lois pour {{contrôler|control}} les critiques à l'étranger.

bd.meaning: China also uses its new laws to control criticism abroad.
chunks: La Chine utilise aussi ses nouvelles lois
China also uses its new laws
bd.key: pour + plain verb, one more time. pour contrôler = “to control” — this “in order to” shape has appeared throughout every story so far.

body.fr: Une loi de juillet {{interdit|forbids}} tout acte, même en dehors de la Chine, qui « nuit à l'unité nationale ».

bd.meaning: A July law forbids any act, even outside China, that 'harms national unity.'
chunks: même en dehors de la Chine
bd.key: “qui” again hooks on a description, this time to “tout acte”: an act THAT harms national unity.

body.fr: Selon des experts, ce mouvement {{montre|shows}} la volonté de la Chine de centraliser son pouvoir.

bd.meaning: According to experts, this movement shows China's desire to centralize its power.
chunks: la volonté de la Chine de centraliser
China's desire to centralize (volonté de + plain verb)
bd.key: “selon” = “according to.” A simple way to attribute an opinion or claim to someone else.

body.fr: En créant ces lois, le gouvernement chinois envoie aussi un message clair aux autres pays.

bd.meaning: By creating these laws, the Chinese government also sends a clear message to other countries.
bd.key: en + -ant form = “by ___ing.” en créant = “by creating” — a new shape worth knowing: it describes how something is done.

body.fr: La Chine ne veut plus être seulement une {{victime|victim}} de l'histoire mondiale.

bd.meaning: China no longer wants to be just a victim of world history.
chunks: La Chine ne veut plus être
China no longer wants to be (ne...plus = no longer)
bd.key: ne … plus, to close this idea. ne veut plus = “no longer wants” — the same sandwich you meet whenever something that used to be true stops being true.

body.fr: Elle veut maintenant {{écrire|write}} les règles elle-même.

bd.meaning: It now wants to write the rules itself.
chunks: it now wants to write (vouloir + plain verb)
bd.key: “elle-même” = “itself/herself.” Add même after a pronoun to emphasize “by itself / on its own.”

grammar.fr: Une directrice a été arrêtée / les banques sont poursuivies
grammar.en: être + past participle = the passive (“was/is ___ed”). Unlike avoir + past participle (the ordinary past), this shape says something was done TO the subject.

grammar.fr: La banque n'est plus... / la Chine ne veut plus...
grammar.en: ne … plus = “no longer / not anymore.” Same sandwich shape as ne … pas, but marks something that used to be true and now isn't.
en + -ant form = “by ___ing.” Describes the means or manner of an action — en créant = “by creating.”

quiz.q: Pourquoi la Chine a-t-elle obligé Meta à annuler l'achat de Manus ?
quiz.a: Parce que la Chine renforce son contrôle sur les technologies d'intelligence artificielle et travaille sur de nouvelles lois pour mieux contrôler ces technologies. (Because China is tightening control over AI technology and working on new laws to better control it.)

flag: This compresses a dense Economist piece with several named legal experts (Henry Gao, Mark Jia, Yalkun Uluyol) and additional laws — the entry/exit-ban rules taking effect in September, the EU-style “blocking statute” comparison, a pending cyber-crime bill, a corruption-evidence law, and older tactics like covert police stations and kidnapped dissidents — all dropped to focus on three concrete threads: the Meta/Manus deal, the JPMorgan/Citigroup lawsuits, and the Samsung/ZTE court clash. The $44m figure is the combined total from the article, not one single lawsuit. tournant (turning point) and long bras (long arm) are natural-sounding choices for ideas the article treats more abstractly — a native speaker might reach directly for the technical term extraterritorialité, which I avoided as too advanced for A1.
